scheme_name: PMMSY: Installation of Cages in Reservoirs Scheme - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to enhance fish production and promote sustainable fisheries. 

This scheme was launched on September 10, 2020. 

The PMMSY aims to achieve a targeted fish production of 22 million metric tons by the year 2024-2025. 

It also seeks to increase the income of fishers and fish farmers by providing them with better access to resources and technology. 

The Installation of Cages in Reservoirs Scheme is a specific component under PMMSY that focuses on enhancing fish production in reservoirs through the installation of cages. 

This initiative is particularly relevant for states like Haryana, which has a growing demand for fish and aquaculture products. 

The primary objective of the Installation of Cages in Reservoirs Scheme is to promote the use of modern aquaculture techniques. 

This includes the installation of floating cages in reservoirs to facilitate the farming of various fish species. 

The scheme aims to increase fish production in reservoirs by utilizing the available water bodies efficiently. 

It also aims to enhance the livelihoods of local fishers by providing them with new opportunities in aquaculture. 

The benefits of this scheme include financial assistance for the installation of cages. 

The government provides a subsidy of up to 40% for the installation of cages in reservoirs. 

For Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, the subsidy can go up to 60%. 

The maximum subsidy amount is capped at INR 1 lakh per beneficiary. 

The scheme also provides assistance for the procurement of quality fish seeds and feed. 

Each beneficiary can receive financial support for the purchase of fish seeds and feed up to INR 50,000. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a resident of Haryana. 

Beneficiaries must be involved in fishing or aquaculture activities. 

There is no specific age limit for applicants. 

However, they must possess a valid identity proof and address proof. 

Additionally, applicants should have a bank account linked to their Aadhar number for the disbursement of subsidies. 

The application process for the Installation of Cages in Reservoirs Scheme is straightforward. 

Interested beneficiaries must submit an application form to the Department of Fisheries in Haryana. 

The application form can be obtained from the official website of the Haryana Fisheries Department. 

Applicants must attach documents such as identity proof, address proof, and bank account details. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

The authorities will conduct a field verification to assess the feasibility of the proposed cage installation. 

After successful verification, the subsidy amount will be sanctioned. 

The disbursement of the subsidy is typically done in two installments. 

The first installment is released after the installation of the cages. 

The second installment is released after the successful stocking of fish seeds. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Fisheries, Government of Haryana. 

The department is responsible for overseeing the entire process from application to disbursement. 

For any queries or assistance, beneficiaries can contact the Department of Fisheries at their official helpline number. 

The helpline number is available on the official website of the Haryana Fisheries Department. 

The Installation of Cages in Reservoirs Scheme is expected to create employment opportunities in the fisheries sector. 

It aims to empower local communities by enhancing their skills in aquaculture. 

The scheme also promotes sustainable fishing practices to ensure the long-term viability of fish stocks. 

The government encourages the use of environmentally friendly practices in cage farming. 

This includes proper waste management and the use of organic feed. 

The scheme is part of a larger effort to boost the Blue Revolution in India. 

The Blue Revolution aims to enhance fish production and promote sustainable fisheries management. 

The PMMSY, including the Installation of Cages in Reservoirs Scheme, is expected to contribute significantly to the overall growth of the fisheries sector in India. 

The scheme also aligns with the government's vision of achieving self-sufficiency in fish production. 

As of 2023, the fisheries sector contributes approximately 1.24% to India's GDP. 

The government aims to increase this contribution through various initiatives under PMMSY. 

The Installation of Cages in Reservoirs Scheme is a crucial step towards achieving this goal. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of research and development in aquaculture. 

The government plans to collaborate with research institutions to improve fish farming techniques. 

This includes the development of disease-resistant fish species and improved feed formulations. 

The scheme is expected to have a positive impact on the nutritional security of the population. 

Fish is a rich source of protein and essential nutrients. 

By increasing fish production, the scheme aims to make fish more accessible to consumers. 

The government also plans to promote fish marketing and value addition. 

This includes establishing fish processing units and cold storage facilities. 

The Installation of Cages in Reservoirs Scheme is an integral part of the broader strategy to enhance the fisheries sector in Haryana. 

It aims to empower local fishers and promote sustainable aquaculture practices. 

The scheme is expected to play a vital role in improving the livelihoods of those dependent on fishing. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the progress of the scheme to ensure its effectiveness. 

Regular updates and reports are published to keep stakeholders informed about the scheme's impact. 

Overall, the Installation of Cages in Reservoirs Scheme under PMMSY represents a significant investment in the future of fisheries in Haryana. 

It reflects the government's commitment to promoting sustainable development in the fisheries sector. 

The scheme is a step towards achieving economic growth while ensuring environmental sustainability. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to create a thriving aquaculture industry that benefits all stakeholders involved. 

This includes fishers, consumers, and the environment alike.
